summary.text: General relativity is Einstein's theory of gravity, published in 1916, which describes gravity as a geometric property of space and time.
In it, the curvature of spacetime is tied to the energy, momentum and stress of whatever is present, so spacetime tells matter how to move and matter tells spacetime how to curve.
It predicts black holes, gravitational lensing and gravitational waves, and all tests so far have agreed with it.

facts.label: Predicted objects
facts.value: Black holes, where nothing, not even light, can escape

facts.label: Gravitational waves
facts.value: Predicted, and observed directly by LIGO and others

facts.label: Open problem
facts.value: No self-consistent theory of quantum gravity has been found

items.prompt: A physicist describes gravity not as a pull across space but as something about the shape of space and time. Which theory is she using?

options.label: Newton's law of universal gravitation
General relativity
Quantum electrodynamics
Geometric optics

items.explain: General relativity provides a description of gravity as a geometric property of space and time.

items.prompt: Wheeler said, 'Space-time tells matter how to move; matter tells space-time how to curve.' What does the second half mean?

options.label: Matter and energy shape the curvature of spacetime
Matter is unaffected by the geometry around it
Spacetime stays flat whatever matter is present
Only light, not matter, can bend spacetime

items.explain: Spacetime curvature is directly related to the energy, momentum and stress of whatever is present, including matter and radiation.

items.prompt: Engineers designing a bridge use Newton's law of gravity and get good results. Why does that not contradict general relativity?

options.label: Because Newton's law is shown to be wrong for all cases
Because bridges are too large for any theory of gravity
Because gravity has no effect on objects near the ground
Because it is the prediction of the theory for nearly flat spacetime

items.explain: Newton's law can be seen as a prediction of general relativity for the almost flat spacetime around stationary mass distributions.

items.prompt: Astronomers see a distant galaxy appear as several distorted copies around a closer cluster. Which prediction of general relativity explains this?

options.label: Gravitational lensing, the bending of light
Quantum tunneling through the cluster
Diffraction of light by a narrow slit
The electroweak unification at high energy

items.explain: General relativity predicts gravitational lensing, where light bending produces distorted and multiple images of the same distant object.

items.prompt: Why do physicists still say gravity is not fully understood, despite general relativity passing every test?

options.label: Because its predictions failed in several experiments
Because it cannot yet be reconciled with quantum physics
Because black holes have never been predicted by it
Because it only applies to stars, not planets

items.explain: All tests have agreed with it, but no self-consistent theory of quantum gravity has been found, so gravity is not yet unified with the other three interactions.

items.prompt: The theory's time-dependent solutions let scientists run the history of the universe backward and forward. What did that help establish?

options.label: The cosmic framework behind the Big Bang and microwave background
The proof that light needs a medium to travel through
The rule that heat always flows from hot to cold
The exact number of atoms in a single molecule

items.explain: These solutions provided the modern framework for cosmology, leading to the discovery of the Big Bang and cosmic microwave background radiation.
